findings.claim: PLO 6287 (1982) ended EO 4364 and EO 5702 by revocation; M5 relies on 43 U.S.C. 1714(j) for refuge persistence
findings.evidence: Held S03 (43 U.S.C. 1714(j)): the Secretary shall not 'modify, or revoke any withdrawal which added lands to the National Wildlife Refuge System prior to October 21, 1976'. EO 5702 (official text) reserved the Port Orford, Blanco and Rogue River reefs as a refuge (WPA: 'reserved as a refuge for the protection of sea lions'); BLM row for PLO 6287 reads 'withdrawing lands for addition to Oregon Islands National Wildlife Refuge; revoking EO Nos. 4082, 4364, 4774 and 5702'. A 1982 secretarial revocation of a pre-1976 refuge withdrawal sits against the very bar the doctrine cites; the doctrine neither notes the conflict nor holds the PLO text that would show its authority or that it is a replacement withdrawal.
findings.fix: Keep B59 at most as no with an added gap stating the 1714(j) question (whether EO 5702's and EO 4364's lands were in the System before 1976 and how PLO 6287 squares with 1714(j)), or hold B59 open until 47 FR 27292 is acquired.

The revocation is by number, verifiable on the web, of the same standing as the web-read sources the doctrine accepts for the B01 and B04 yes leads.
findings.fix: Add a no/ACT branch for EO 779, fixed 1935-01-04 (Proclamation 2112, 49 Stat. 3430, to be verified on acquisition), with the gap that the proclamation text is read on the web; or at least state in the gap that the revocation is confirmed on the web and list the acquisition.

findings.location: B04 gap and md on EO 5095
findings.claim: EO 5095's link to the Nunivak Island Reservation rests on the island name alone
findings.evidence: The held EO 5095 title is 'Reserving Certain Described Lands for Agricultural Experimentation Station Purposes and for Establishment of Nunivak Island Reser[vation]'; EO 5470 (held member) adds adjacent islands 'to and made part of the Nunivak Island Reservation'; PLO 1177 (BLM table) revokes 'in part ... No. 5095 of Apr. 15, 1929'. The link is stronger than stated. Separately, EO 5095 is a mixed order (reindeer, caribou and musk-ox experiments for the Agriculture Department as well as a bird and game preserve), and the doctrine does not say whether sec. 305 ('with respect to units of the National Wildlife Refuge System') keeps the whole order or only its refuge part.
findings.fix: State the EO 5470 and title links; add a gap that EO 5095 also has non-refuge purposes whose continuation sec. 305 may not reach.

findings.claim: sec. 303 'incorporates the existing ... Nunivak refuge into the Yukon Delta NWR'; sec. 305 at 94 Stat. 2394-2395
findings.evidence: NPS ANILCA_508.pdf (https://www.nps.gov/subjects/wilderness/upload/ANILCA_508.pdf) prints sec. 303(7)(A) as 'The Yukon Delta National Wildlife Refuge shall consist of the existing Clarence Rhode National Wildlife Range, Hazen Bay National Wildlife Refuge, and Nunivak National Wildlife Refuge ...' and places sec. 305 after the '94 STAT. 2395' marker; the sec. 305 wording quoted by the doctrine matches. The FWS Alaska Maritime NWR legal description (https://www.fws.gov/r7/nwr/Realty/data/LegalDocuments/FR/Alaska-Maritime-NWR.pdf) confirms sec. 303(1) names 'the existing' Chamisso, Bering Sea, Pribilof (Walrus and Otter Islands), Aleutian Islands, Bogoslof, Forrester Island, Hazy Islands, Saint Lazaria and Tuxedni refuges unit by unit and lists EO 1037, 1039, 1040, 1044, 1049, 1458, 1459, 1658 and 5318 as establishing orders. ANILCA remains unheld; govinfo was not reachable from this session.
findings.fix: Quote 303(7)(A) as 'shall consist of the existing ... Nunivak National Wildlife Refuge'; give sec. 305 as 94 Stat. 2395 (to be confirmed in the Statutes at Large); add the FWS legal description as a supporting crosswalk source to acquire.

findings.claim: Pub. L. 100-226 sec. 3 directs that the refuges 'established ... by Executive orders dated October 23, 1907, as amended' be administered as refuges

findings.claim: 'A text check requires a revoking or reducing word in the member's own text'
findings.evidence: The condition is any_regex, which also matches the title and WPA summary. EO 347A's held text (OCR) has no such word ('Ganeele@' for 'cancelled'); it passes only through its WPA summary ('revoked in so far as it applies').

findings.claim: 'Before 1976 the 1966 Act let the Secretary revoke refuge withdrawals, which is why so many PLO revocations fall in 1947-1975'
findings.evidence: Held 668dd amendment note: the 1976 amendment struck a sentence preserving 'the authority of the Secretary to modify or revoke public land withdrawals affecting lands in the System'; the 1966 Act preserved an authority that came from presidential delegation (PLOs began in 1942, before the Act). The causal 'which is why' is not shown by any source cited.
findings.fix: Say the 1966 Act preserved the Secretary's existing (delegated) authority to revoke withdrawals until the 1976 amendment struck that sentence; drop the causal clause.

summary: The engine run reproduces the stated counts (243 members, 87 decided, 5 flagged). Every held pin and sha256 checks out, all 30 PLO rows match the BLM tables, and the yes-lead predicates (Pub. L. 100-226 sec. 3, 50 CFR 216.85, 43 U.S.C. 1787(b)(4), ANILCA secs. 303 and 305) say what the doctrine says, subject to small wording and scope fixes. Three errors need correcting before adoption. B10 dates EO 4832 to 1928-03-07 when it is March 17, 1928. S04 cites Proclamation 2416 at 54 Stat. 2771 when it is 2717. EO 375A is left open although the held EO 5750 revokes it in full by date and land description. B59 rests two no leads on a 1982 PLO without addressing the 43 U.S.C. 1714(j) bar the doctrine itself cites. EO 779's revocation by Proclamation 2112 is verifiable on the web. The other findings are disclosure and consistency fixes.
